newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Foschini year earnings seen lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Foschini year earnings seen lower.

text.p: Clothing retailer Foschini Group Ltd is seen posting a slide in year earnings, knocked by a weak retail sector and high consumer debt levels, analysts said on Wednesday.
"They made a decision to curtail credit because of a tough trading credit market and this has affected the top line," said Eric Levine, an analyst at Investec Securities.
"Margins are under pressure, and American Swiss and Sterns have also had a difficult trading time," he told Reuters.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings per share for the year ended March 31 falling to between 93.1 and 105.0 cents with consensus at 98.1 cents from 112.8 cents a year ago.
Foschini, which is due to announce results next Wednesday, awards capitalisation shares instead of a cash dividend.
One analyst who declined to be identified said that Foschini had also been losing market share to other retailers.
Its offshore operations, represented by its effective control of Oceana Investment Corp Plc would also depress earnings, analysts said.

Losses at womenswear retailer Etam Plc, the main contributer to Oceana's earnings, deepened in the year to January 25 to an after-tax loss of 4.22 million stg compared with a 0.24 million loss a year ago.

Foschini's share price has shrunk by 58 percent from a peak of 31.89 rand on January 14 to a low of 13.25 rand on May 30 as investors anticipated weak results. At 1045 GMT on Wednesday it stood at 13.70 rand -- up 20 cents on the day.
The share price has underperformed the industrial index by 55 percent since the beginning of the financial year under review.
But analysts said that it was seen as fairly valued at its current levels and looked interesting on a two-year view.
